title: Canonical mate factorization on the explicit affine alternating Cech model
statement: Fix shared derived categories [def-pc-derived-category], rings A,B, a quasi-compact separated f:X -> Spec A and g:Spec B -> Spec A. Let U:Fin r -> X.Opens be an affine cover, G a quasi-coherent O_X-module, and c a comparison specified by [def-pc-derived-module-base-change-map]. Put K equal to the explicit model [def-pc-affine-alternating-cech-model]. There exist the ordinary tensor-pullback functor F for g (pinned on objects and maps), a left-derived counit epsilon for [def-pc-derived-pullback], an isomorphism e:Rf_*G[0] -> Qh(K), and an isomorphism t:Qh(F(K)) -> Rf_B,*((p*G)[0]), such that the canonical mate [def-pc-derived-base-change-map] followed by Rf_B,*(c) equals Lg*(e.hom) followed by epsilon at K followed by t.hom. No flatness of G or K is assumed and no invertibility of epsilon is asserted.

proof.text: Use the fixed family delta of left-derived counits and its additive tensor-pullback instances from the derived composition theorem. Define c0 by delta_p at the single complex followed by the single-complex identification. It satisfies IsDerivedModulePullbackComparison by its definition. The fixed-counit Cech theorem provides e,t and the mate equation for c0.
Apply the target-automorphism theorem to c0 and the caller-supplied c, obtaining alpha:p*G isomorphic to p*G with c=c0 followed by alpha[0].

Take F to be the actual tensorPullback g functor; the pinned object equations are reflexivity and the map equations simplify identities. Keep delta_g and e, and replace t with t followed by RfB_*(alpha[0]). Functoriality, the equation for c0, and associativity give exactly the required equation for c. Functors preserve isomorphisms, so this is still an isomorphism. No invertibility of delta_g at K is used.

proof_origin.place: Steps 2--5; formal combination of the fixed-counit Cech calculation and Step 4 target-automorphism argument
